deltas.behavior_text: The guest mail budget is taken in the background send task just before the send, not on the request before scheduling it (independent review: equal request-path work for every address). A code whose mail the budget refused, or whose send failed, is revoked at once.

The all-mail ceiling keeps its last quarter for approved users' sign-in codes and notices, and a ceiling refusal counts in failed_sends and raises a 'ceiling' alert. The ceiling is per process and resets on restart; the guest budget is the persistent limit.
Only outage failures (classified kinds) feed the failed_sends threat rule; recipient errors and ceiling refusals do not, so a bad address never raises a rule alert either.

Each guest may use at most a tenth of the validator's daily cap; validator calls run in their own two-thread pool and a call past its timeout blocks that guest's next calls (unchecked) until it ends; a blocked line answers 422 so the refused-responses rule doesn't count it; a flagged line is stored once as a review record and kept out of the training export.
Live rollout sets threat_rules.entry_posts to 20 instead of the plan's starting 10, because one guest's sign-in is about 4 entry posts and 10 would alert on three ordinary sign-ins.
The reserved-domain check also refuses a trailing-dot domain and address literals such as a@[127.0.0.1].
